title: Argue, Summarise, and Write Formally
subject: inggris
summary: Past perfect, third conditional, modal passive, inversion, argumentative texts, summaries, survey bias, and formal emails.
objectives: use the past perfect and the third conditional
use modal passives and inversion after negative phrases
find the claim, reasons, and counterargument in an argumentative text
write a short summary that keeps the main contrast

sections.title: Earlier in the past
sections.html:
Use the past perfect for the earlier of two past actions: By the time we arrived, the film had already started.

Third conditionalIf + had + past participle, would have + past participle
If she had studied, she would have passed.

sections.title: Passive and inversion
sections.html: Modal passive: The rules must be followed. Inversion after negative openers: Not only did she pass the exam, but she also got the highest score. Other openers: never, rarely, hardly.

sections.title: Reading an argument
sections.html: An argumentative or hortatory text has a claim, reasons with evidence, often a counterargument (the other side), and a rebuttal that answers it. Signal words: some people argue, however, nevertheless, therefore.

sections.title: Summarising
sections.html: A good summary is short, uses your own words, and keeps the main idea and the key contrast. Leave out examples and small details. Avoid adding opinions that are not in the text.

sections.title: Formal writing
sections.html:
Use full words, polite indirect requests, and a clear purpose: "I would be grateful if you could ...", "Could you please ...", "I look forward to hearing from you." Avoid chat abbreviations like u and ur.

When judging a survey, ask who answered it. An online poll on one website represents that website's visitors, not everyone.
